claims.statement: The prototype completed three Poki tests with 500 gameplays in each test.
The retained summary records an earlier 44-second baseline, while the Poki dashboard directly confirms the final 1 minute 53 second result.
The project included order, reward, countdown, vehicle-upgrade, area-unlock, onboarding, and multimodal feedback work.
The three visible completed versions averaged 1 minute 14 seconds, 1 minute 46 seconds, and 1 minute 53 seconds across 500 gameplays each.
The supplied runtime image shows a third-person driving view with delivery, timer, currency, pickup, and pause UI.
Retained Week 8 playtests identified difficult handling, excessive obstacles, shop friction, and missed keyboard and Shift controls.
Mentor feedback identified UI overload, steering jitter, and a 50 to 60 MB WebGL build as iteration concerns.
The UI and handling feedback document most likely corresponds to the transition from the Week 9 build to the Week 10 simplification pass.
The Week 10 record removes the landing and Start screens, character and pop-up tutorials, the first-delivery pop-up, and the damage pop-up.

decisions.decision: Frame the case study around behaviour-led iteration rather than feature count.
decisions.rationale: The strongest available evidence is the three-round playtime change.

decisions.decision: Introduce Normal, Rush, and VIP orders gradually rather than exposing all variants at the start.
decisions.rationale: Early orders could teach the base loop before adding urgency and higher rewards.

decisions.decision: Replace repeated tutorial screens and pop-ups with prompts positioned closer to the car and current objective.
decisions.rationale: Mentor feedback and playtests showed that additional explanation was competing with the task itself.

timeline.event: Developed and iterated the tutorial and first level during the internship.
Integrated Poki and documented the delivery economy, damage, repairs, vehicles, and zone unlocks.
Playtesting surfaced handling, obstacle, shop, keyboard, Shift, and zombie-spawn friction.
Expanded staged order types, zone-specific deliveries, damage feedback, garage onboarding, and terrain progression.
Simplified the opening and tutorials, removed several pop-ups, and moved essential prompts into the play space.

gaps: Original dashboard evidence for the earlier 44-second baseline
Causal attribution between individual changes and playtime
Explicit dates and build identifiers for the two mentor feedback documents
Final build size and steering-jitter verification
Player sample and observation method for qualitative playtest notes
Clear ownership boundary for art assets and team contributions
assumptions: The audience is an English-speaking game design or Unity hiring manager.
